newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Telkom says no telephones for new firm.
newsitem.headline: Telkom says no telephones for new firm.

text.p: PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia (Telkom) said on Thursday the products to be offered by a new multi-media firm link to a well-connected businessmen did not include telephone services.
"The new company's services do not include telephone services, I repeat, do not include telephone services," Telkom's President Director Asman Akhir Nasution told analysts in a conference call.

Nasution was refering to questions after local media reports said the new company, linked to President Suharto's brother-in-law Sudwikatmono, would be allowed to provide basic telephone services including local and domestic long distance calls.
Telkom said it recently negotiated a joint venture agreement with privately-owned PT Indocitra Grahabawana linked to Sudwikatmono.
The new venture, PT Multimedia Nusantara, also has ties with Indosat's, subsidiary PT Indosat Mega Media and a foundation belonging to state television broadcaster TVRI.
Telkom said in a statement on Thursday the new firm's primary focus would be on providing multimedia services throughout Indonesia.
It said the new firm will be 49 percent owned by Indocitra, 31 percent by Telkom, 15 percent by Indosat subsidiary and five percent by TVRI.
Nasution said multi-media would offer good future earnings prospects for Telkom.
Nevetherless, Telkom did not take the majority stakeholding and would reconsider the size of its stake in the future, he said.
